title: Dimensions of an extended completed toric pair
statement: Let B be a Noetherian local ring, T a sharp fs commutative monoid, J contained in the maximal ideal of B, and mixed a Boolean. Suppose AddMonoidAlgebra.HasExtendedFormalMonoidModel B (Additive T) J mixed holds: its one nonzero complete regular local coefficient ring D presents the completed pair, with its parameter reduction in m_D minus m_D squared in the mixed case. Then ModelDimensions B T J mixed holds, with the same meaning and the same coefficient ring throughout as defined in def-trf-formal-chart-geometric-data. Thus it retains the pair presentation, asserts regularity of the completed quotient by J, and computes both completed dimensions with e=0 or e=1. This conclusion concerns completions only, not regularity or dimensions before completion or after strict henselization.

proof.text: Unpack the extended formal model. Under the canonical evaluation equivalence for polynomials in zero variables, its completed monoid ring and monomial ideal become the objects of formal-monoid-ring-dimension. Apply that theorem to the sharp fs monoid T and D. In the field-model case its stratum equivalence identifies the quotient with D and gives its dimension.

In the mixed case the D-algebra stratum equivalence of the dimension theorem equals the specified rho: the constant inclusion D -> H/L is surjective and each equivalence is its inverse. Apply its parameter clause to eta, using rho(eta) in m_D minus m_D squared. Quotienting H/(eta) by the image of L is the same as quotienting H/L by the class of eta, so its stratum is D/(rho(eta)). The dimension theorem gives both dimension drops by one and regular-local regularity of the latter.

A regular local ring is regular as a ring. Transport regularity and Krull dimensions through the pair isomorphism, and retain D, its completeness, and the original pair map. Discard only the residue-field equivalence and adic-topology assertions of the extended model, which ModelDimensions does not request.
